lead: American painter (1856-1925), born in Florence, who worked in Paris, London and Venice; known for black-based portraits and bright, quick watercolors.
paras: John Singer Sargent was born in Florence to American parents and trained in Paris under Carolus-Duran. He built his career on portraits in Paris and then London, and from the 1900s painted more landscapes and watercolors while traveling.
The chapters below follow him from Paris to the London portrait trade and on to the quick watercolors, and end with what the archive shows.

chapters.title: Paris and a black dress
chapters.text:
Sargent studied with Carolus-Duran, a teacher who trained pupils to place tones directly and quickly. The habit shows in his deep blacks set against pale cloth and skin: a dress of white or silver beside a coat of near-black.

The famous example is his 1884 portrait of Madame Gautreau, whose pale skin against a black dress caused talk at the Salon. He left Paris for London soon afterward.

chapters.title: London portraits
chapters.text:
In England he became a leading portraitist of the well-off, painting with a fluent brush that kept the whites from going flat. In a Sargent they are rarely pure: they carry blue, {{Rose}} or green from the room around them.

He also painted garden pictures such as Carnation, Lily, Lily, Rose, worked outdoors at dusk in short sessions, and these give a quieter, greener {{Sage}} next to the portrait blacks.

chapters.title: Travel watercolors
chapters.when: Venice, the Alps, the Middle East · 1900s
chapters.text:
In his travel watercolors, around Venice, the Alps and the Middle East, he left white paper to carry the light and worked quickly in transparent washes. Compare a portrait ground with one of these sheets and it can look like two painters.

The sheets lean on {{Azure}} and {{Powder Blue}} for water and shade, where the portraits lean on black.
chapters.pull: Compare a portrait with a watercolor and it can look like two painters.

chapters.title: What our archive shows
chapters.text:
Our archive holds 610 Sargent paintings, photographs of varnished surfaces, so these are approximate. Black and {{Raisin Black}} are his signature colors, used about twice as much as by his peers.

{{Smoky Black}} is his darkest large area, covering at least 3% of the canvas in 148 paintings, and his lightest are Ecru, greyish white and Oatmeal.
